title: March 1942 Decca session with a studio group
summary: They listen to 'Beside the River Clyde'; Maxine says the discographies are wrong and the date was put together by Decca, not Billy Kyle.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: But! When you come to the March the 19th, 1942 session that you recorded -- now in both the Rust discography and Bruyninckx's, it says the personnel is the same as the previous sessions. And on that date, you recorded 'Beside The River Clyde' and 'How Do I Know It's Real'.
Yes.
And on both of those, it sounds to me like a big band, or certainly an augmented group, and there's certainly a string section behind that.
I haven't heard those, and I don't recall just what -- you know, what it
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
We can play them if you like.
Yeah, I'd like to hear those, because I don't have them myself.

All right, we're back on tape again. We've just been listening to the "Beside The River Clyde" and "How Do I Know It's Real." Quite evidently, these are studio groups. Whereas in the discography, they're listed as being the same personnel as all your sessions which was by the John Kirby Band. Now --

But it's not. This group of selections were made for Decca under the direction of Peter van Steeden, who was the director for Decca. And I imagined he had access to musicians, and he just called them in. And he made the arrangements and everything.
Yeah.
But I don't recall any of the musicians except on one of the records, there's
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
a little piano that looked like it might be -- sounded like it might be Billy Kyle.
But the session was not gotten together by Billy. It was definitely put together by Peter van Steeden.
Yeah.

Well these two sides -- beside these two records -- 'Beside the River Clyde' and How Do I Know It's Real,' quite obviously by a studio group; the ones before sound like they could be made by the Kirby Band or a similar combination of instruments.
You're saying, in fact, that this was --
The instrumentation was the same, yeah. I imagine that they felt they had to keep that instrumentation to get that little tight sound, but it was definitely not Kirby's group.
So you're, saying the discographies are definitely wrong on that point as far as all these Decca sides are concerned?
Yes.
Okay.
This -- let me see, where were we. Okay.
